content:
Ha, that previuos message is already out of date, since we now have vcgen, and I pushed Claude some more towards the level of robust automation I’d expect:

con-ron: Theorem 1's proofs moved to vcgen + grind in SymM

con-ron's Theorem 1 relates the arena-based checker (a Lean twin of the Rust code) to con-leche's pure functions. It consists of a few thousand Hoare-triple simulation proofs, one per walk. Until recently they were proved with vcgen followed by hand-written case analysis on the verification conditions (case vc15 => rename_i …). That broke on every con-leche sync, because one extra call shifts every condition's number and every hypothesis's position. A first attempt replaced this with a custom closer (bridge_auto, ~2 000 lines of MetaM). It was robust, but it was a pile of goal-family-specific search steps.

Now every walk proof has the same shape:

theorem whnfBody_spec … : ⦃fun s => s = s₀⦄ whnfBody … ⦃fun r s' => …; ⊤⦄ := by
  sym only [bridge_grind] => vcgen [whnfBody, callee specs…] <;> finish

vcgen runs inside grind's symbolic mode, so each verification condition's hypotheses go straight into one shared E-graph and finish closes them there. No custom tactic runs between vcgen and grind, and nothing addresses goals by position. The mathematics lives in a ~1 100-line vocabulary of @[bridge_grind] lemmas:

  • store extension is a preorder, Ext as ≤, so grind's order solver handles the store chains;
  • carrying a denotation along a store extension is one equation;
  • callee answers are named predicates (Ans, MapRel) rather than funs, since lambdas inside atoms trigger grind's funext case splits;
  • witnesses are stated as equations over the denotation functions, with no ∃ in postconditions;
  • multi-patterns that would pair unrelated terms carry a grind_pattern … where guard ….

These lemma-style rules turned out to be what makes grind fast and predictable. Before them, the same goals under plain grind cost 100× more.

Before (custom closers and position-addressed conditions) → now, over all of Theorem 1 (~116 files, comment and blank lines excluded):

before now
meta code (macro/elab/tactics) 427 229 −46 %
lemma vocabulary for grind 0 1 105 new
proof bodies (:= by …) 47 285 41 876 −11 %
statements / definitions 20 055 21 036 +5 %
elaboration, wall time (2 runs each) 592 / 615 s 228 / 216 s ≈2.7× faster
elaboration, instructions:u 5 677 G 1 647 G 3.4× fewer

The meta code that remains is a few macros in parts of the proof that aren't stated as Hoare triples. Along the way we found one grind bug: a hypothesis that merely has the shape of a match condition gets silently taken out of E-matching, so the result depends on hypothesis order (lean4#15697).

First sync under the new style. We then synced con-leche's latest changes: arguments compared last to first, the eagerReduce mode with its own knot slot, and unbounded fuel. Theorem 1 changed by +335/−54 lines in 11 files, about 8 minutes of build time from the first build to green. Every edit was either a statement that genuinely changed or a new lemma; no existing proof broke while its mathematics stayed the same. The nicest data point is defeqSpine_spec: its statement changed (it now compares reversed spines), but its proof text did not, because the change went into the one equation the vocabulary keeps for con-leche's function, plus two facts about reverse. Two of the four new walk proofs closed on the first try. The previous sync, under the old style, had touched 100 files (+8 373/−15 249) and had to renumber 301 case vcN arms. The two syncs aren't directly comparable, though: the old one removed a whole data representation, and this one didn't move any walk's verification conditions without also changing its statement. The remaining exposure is a handful of proofs still written step by step by hand, which restate con-leche's guards in their text. Every edit to an existing proof in this sync was in one of those, and converting them is the next step.
